function: MU-MIMO downlink precoding (network maps CSI to the auxiliary tensors of the closed-form WMMSE precoder) and learned user scheduling (p. 8-9).
system: Massive MIMO downlink: BS dual-polarized UPA with N_T = 32 antennas (24-40 tested), K = 8 users with N_R = 2 antennas, 3.5 GHz, no RIS (p. 9-10).
method: Permutation-equivariant NNs (TEPN, TEUSN) built from tensor-equivariant modules; precoding unsupervised on sum-rate loss, scheduling supervised on greedy labels; Adam (p. 8-9).
data_channel: QuaDRiGa simulator, 3GPP 38.901 UMa NLOS at 3.5 GHz, 60,000 channels per dataset: 55,000 train, 5,000 test; scheduling labels from greedy algorithm (p. 9).
test_conditions: Trained at N_T=32, K=8, N_R=2 over SNRs 0-40 dB; tested directly with N_T 24-40 and K 6-10 (precoding), N_T and candidate users 10-14 (scheduling) (p. 9, 11, 12).
baselines: Non-learned: ZF, MMSE, WMMSE (random or MMSE init), random and greedy scheduling; learned: GNN, DNN, CNN precoders (p. 10, 12).
metrics: Average sum-rate (bits/channel use) versus SNR, N_T, K and training-set size; multiplications, FLOPs and parameter counts (p. 10-12).
complexity: Complexity orders and real multiplications in Tables I-II (TECFP 1.0e6 vs WMMSE-MMSEInit 3.1e7, N_T=32, K=8), FLOPs and parameters versus N_T (p. 10-12).
openness: Code released at https://github.com/ZJSXYZ/TENN (p. 1); channels generated with QuaDRiGa, no dataset link.
q1_support: p. 9: "utilize QuaDRiGa channel simulator to generate all channel data"; p. 9: "38.901 UMa NLOS"
q2_support: p. 11: "We train our network in scenario NT = 32, K = 8, NR = 2 and directly apply it to various different scenarios"
q3_support: p. 10: "Conventional algorithms for iterative solving of the sum-rate maximization precoding problem [4]"; p. 10: "The AI-aided approach utilizing GNN for computation of precoding tensors from CSI [36]". Also DNN [13] and CNN [49]; sum-rate compared in Fig. 5.
q4_support: p. 10: "Table I contrasts the computational complexities of several methods"
q5_support: p. 1: "Code is available on-line at https://github.com/ZJSXYZ/TENN"
notes: Two tasks: precoding (area 3, main) and user scheduling (above the physical layer), both learned and combined in Section V-C (TECFP-TEUS, p. 12), so the work passes above_phy. The equivariance framework is generic; RIS appears only as a possible future device type (p. 8), so ris = 0. Scheduling is compared only with random and greedy baselines (p. 12); the learned precoding baselines (GNN, DNN, CNN) carry q3.
